notable_absence.finding: No role:/privilege: concept is cited anywhere on this page for who may RUN setting-ldap - only the generic 'unauthorized error' boilerplate shared by every subcommand in this batch. Given that configuring LDAP touches the external authentication domain and, per idp:ldap's own registry description, resolves to Server's local role/group catalogue, the absence of an explicit role citation here (contrast with, say, a Security Admin or User Admin role) is a real gap, not just boilerplate thinness - this is exactly the kind of security-settings command the round's RBAC-citation-consistency hypothesis is watching for, and here the finding is total absence rather than a wrong citation.

cross_component_finding: The SYNOPSIS spells the depth-limiting flag `--nested-group-max-depth`, but the OPTIONS section documents it as `--nested-groups-max-depth` (extra 's' on 'groups') - a literal spelling drift between the two sections of the same page, on the same page that also defines the sibling flag `--enable-nested-groups` (correctly pluralised) immediately above it. A reader copying the flag name from SYNOPSIS would get an option the OPTIONS section never defines under that spelling. This is a second, independent instance (after setting-master-password.md's --rotate-password/--rotate-data-key mismatch) of exactly the SYNOPSIS-vs-OPTIONS drift this round's hypothesis predicts for lightly-reviewed CLI reference content.
cross_product_finding: n/a - no Capella/Mobile/SDK content; idp:ldap's own registry note already states Server's LDAP integration resolves to its own local role/group catalogue, not Capella's sso:realm family, and nothing on this page contradicts or adds to that.
